title: Bitternut Hickory: Ancient Bitternut Hickories You Can Visit
meta_description: A tall, slim hickory of eastern North America. Cook County ranks one in Thatcher Woods at 34.1 metres, and Ottawa's went in about 1886 to 1890.
intro: Bitternut hickory is a hickory of eastern North American woods, and it is a tree we rarely get to show. Two of ours are in the Forest Preserves of Cook County, measured in autumn 2023. The one in Thatcher Woods stands 34.1 metres tall on a trunk only 1.92 metres round, a tall, slim build. The one in Bunker Hill Woods is stouter and shorter, 2.44 metres round and 24.4 metres tall, with a crown about 14 metres across, and the register ranks it second. The third is in Ottawa's Dominion Arboretum, where it was planted sometime between 1886 and 1890, a four-year window that makes it roughly 138 years old. Of the three, the Chicago trees have measurements and no history, while the Ottawa tree has a history and no recorded measurements.
